# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

package net.officefloor.hq.app.claim;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.AuditUser;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.period.PeriodRepository;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.person.PersonGradeRepository;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.person.PersonRepository;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.rate.RateRepository;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.role.Role;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.role.RoleRepository;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.sheet.Sheet;
import net.officefloor.plugin.variable.Val;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestHeader;

/**
 * Re-settles a SETTLED claim: freezes its due again at the figure it would have today as an open claim bound by no
 * statement (today's rates, grades, floor and late charge; n/a leaves it live). Only a steward re-settles, and a claim
 * dated in a closed period, or in any other status, cannot be. Returns the due it had before, for the audit.
 */
public class ApplyResettle {
    public Resettled apply(@Val Claim claim, @Val Sheet sheet, ClaimRepository repository, PersonRepository people,
            RateRepository rates, PersonGradeRepository grades, PeriodRepository periods, RoleRepository roles,
            @RequestHeader(name = "X-User", required = false) String userHeader)
            throws ClaimStatusException, ClerkLimitException {
        String user = AuditUser.decode(userHeader);
        if (periods.isClosedOn(claim.getSheetId(), claim.getDate())) {
            throw new ClaimStatusException("A claim in a closed period cannot be re-settled.");
        }
        if (!Role.STEWARD.equals(roles.roleOf(claim.getSheetId(), user))) {
            throw new ClerkLimitException("Only a steward can re-settle a claim.");
        }
        if (claim.getStatus() != ClaimStatus.SETTLED) {
            throw new ClaimStatusException("A " + claim.getStatus() + " claim cannot be re-settled.");
        }
        BigDecimal old = claim.getDue();
        BigDecimal due = people.findById(claim.getPersonId())
                .map(p -> new ClaimFigures(rates.findBySheetIdOrderByGradeAscFromDateAscIdAsc(claim.getSheetId()),
                        grades.gradesOf(p), sheet).openDue(claim))
                .orElse(null);
        claim.setDue(due);
        repository.saveAndFlush(claim);
        return new Resettled(old, due);
    }
}

A steward can now cancel a person's last statement, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works**
- **New endpoint:** `PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/unstate`, defined in `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/unstate.PUT.yml`. It runs the same steps as taking a statement, except the middle step is `statement/CancelStatement.java`.
  - If the user isn't a steward, it's refused with a 403. If the person has no statement, it's refused with a 400. Either way nothing is written to the store or the audit file.
  - Otherwise it deletes the person's last statement and makes their claims live again. No schema change was needed: taking a statement already binds or unbinds every one of the person's claims, so any claim that is bound now was bound by the last one. That also means a figure from an earlier statement isn't restored.
  - The person's row then shows the statement before it (or nothing), and the count drops by one.
- **Audit:** `statement/AuditStatementCancelled.java` writes `STATEMENT_CANCELLED sheet=… by=… name=… due-total=…` with the cancelled statement's total. The usual `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS` lines follow only when the figures actually change, which is what the test expects.
- **Front end:** in `features/statements/statement.slot.tsx` I added a "Cancel statement" button (`person-unstate`) next to the Statement button. A refusal shows the row's `person-error`, and the error clears on the next action on that row.

**A second fix, outside this feature:** scenario 3 failed because of an existing bug in `period/AutoClosePeriods.java`. When grace days are set and the sheet's today moves past a period, a period that was already soft-closed got closed again. That re-fixed its totals at the new date (10.50 instead of 10.00). The test expects a soft-closed period to stay soft-closed with its totals unchanged, so auto-close now skips soft-closed periods.
